You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life.  When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident.  Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision. Rear camera - Watching your back!  The rear camera helps you see obstacles and hazards you otherwise couldn't by showing enhanced images of what is behind you. The rear camera is an extra set of eyes that's both convenient and safe. Lane departure prevention - Keep it between the lines. It only takes a moment of inattention for your vehicle to drift.  With lane departure prevention, your vehicle takes corrective action to help you avoid unintentionally moving out of your lane. description: Having broomed its sedans from its 2020 model-year lineup, Buick is nearly an all-SUV brand. It is even adding one more to the mix: the all-new 2020 Buick Encore GX. It shares a name with the current Encore extra-small crossover SUV, and the distinctions start getting a little murky from there. The current Encore has been on sale since 2013, which is a long time in car years. But rather than simply introducing a second-generation Encore, Buick has decided to name its successor the Encore GX and sell the two vehicles side by side. The Encore GX is slightly larger, and the two SUVs cost almost the same price. Unless you absolutely cant stretch your budget, the Encore GX is the way to go here. It is by far the superior vehicle thanks to its more robust set of features and more modern cabin designEdmunds Encore GX offers a number of ways to keep you connected. More importantly, the seamless integration of these technologies helps you keep your eyes on the road. AMAZON ALEXA BUILT- IN For the first time ever, the same voice-activated functionality available on Alexa devices at home is now available in Encore GX. For example, you can listen to music, make a phone call with your Bluetooth-connected phone,  get directions sent directly to the available embedded Connected Navigationif properly equipped and even control your compatible smart home devices  to do things like turn on the lights or adjust the thermostat.    Buick Encore GX empowers you with available technologies that help raise your awareness of the road around you. description: 2020 Nissan Kicks SV  Big Personality. Small Gas Bill. Absolutely No Financial Regrets. There are two types of car buyers.  The first wants 400 horsepower, a massive SUV, and a monthly payment that requires a second source of income.  The second wants something stylish, economical, loaded with technology, and smart enough to leave money in the bank.  Meet the 2020 Nissan Kicks SV. Clearly, Nissan had the second buyer in mind.  With its distinctive floating-roof design, bold front grille, and sporty proportions, the Kicks has the personality of a much more expensive crossover.  And here's the beauty of it: This little Nissan knows exactly what it is.  Under the hood, a 1.6L 4-cylinder engine delivers 122 horsepower, paired with Nissan's Xtronic CVT transmission.  Will it outrun a Corvette? Absolutely not.  But with an EPA-estimated 31 MPG city and 36 MPG highway, there's a good chance you'll pass that Corvette while its owner is filling up for the third time.  The SV Trim? Nissan Packed in Some Surprisingly Good Stuff. - 17-Inch Alloy Wheels  Sharp styling without trying too hard. - 7-Inch Touchscreen Display  Convenient technology right at your fingertips. - Apple CarPlay & Android Auto  Your music, navigation apps, and favorite connections along for the ride. - Intelligent Cruise Control  A welcome companion on long highway drives. - Blind Spot Warning  Because knowing what's beside you is generally a good idea. - Rear Cross Traffic Alert  Particularly useful when backing out between oversized pickup trucks. - Automatic Emergency Braking  Intelligent safety technology designed to help avoid certain collisions. - Remote Engine Start  A wonderful invention for anyone who's experienced a Texas summer. - Intelligent Key with Push-Button Start  Convenience that makes everyday life easier. - Automatic Climate Control  Set your temperature and let the car handle the details. - Flexible Rear Cargo Space  Luggage, shopping bags, and everything your weekend requires. And Here's Where the Kicks Really Makes Sense.  It's compact enough to slip into parking spaces that make larger SUVs nervous.  Its elevated seating position gives you a confident view of the road, and the cabin offers surprisingly good passenger room for such a small vehicle.  It's comfortable, easy to drive, and refreshingly uncomplicated.  Sometimes the best car isn't the one with the most horsepower. It's the one that makes the most sense for your life.  The 2020 Nissan Kicks SV is proof that you can have style, useful technology, great fuel economy, and crossover versatility without volunteering your entire paycheck.  The Bottom Line?  This isn't a car designed to impress people at a country club.  It's designed to impress the person who actually pays for it.  And there's something rather satisfying about that.  Come see this smart little crossover at Gulliver Auto Group.  No Haggle. No Hassle. No Games.  The price you see is the price you pay. No surprise charges.  Just a great Nissan, a straightforward price, and a buying experience that makes as much sense as the vehicle itself.  Because looking like a million bucks shouldn't require spending anywhere close to it. Safety and Security Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety.  Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision. Rear camera - Watching your back!  The rear camera helps you see obstacles and hazards you otherwise couldn't by showing enhanced images of what is behind you. The rear camera is an extra set of eyes that's both convenient and safe. Lane departure prevention - Keep it between the lines. It only takes a moment of inattention for your vehicle to drift.  With lane departure prevention, your vehicle takes corrective action to help you avoid unintentionally moving out of your lane.  Lane departure prevention is an extra level of safety for you and those around you.Technology and Telematics Smart device mirroring - Smartphone, meet smart car.
